notes: Pigment-to-manuscript links taken from published technical analyses.

'sources' (top level) defines each reference once under a short key. A manuscript entry cites one with 'source': '<key>' and optional 'source_detail' (e.g. 'Table 1'). A pigment's own 'sources' list holds general references by key.
There are no formulas here because those are your own paint recipes; add them in the admin.
Names match existing pigments (Red Ochre, Azurite, Yellow Ochre), so their manuscript links are added to them instead of creating duplicates.
Re-running fills in a missing source on links that already exist; it never replaces a source that is already set.

pigments.name: Orpiment
pigments.description: Arsenic sulphide (As2S3), a brilliant and poisonous yellow. It is the dominant yellow of the Insular manuscripts and was mixed with indigo to make the green called vergaut.

manuscripts.name: Book of Kells
manuscripts.notes: Yellow.

manuscripts.name: Book of Durrow
manuscripts.notes: Yellow.

manuscripts.name: Book of Armagh
manuscripts.notes: Yellow.

manuscripts.name: Lindisfarne Gospels
manuscripts.notes: Yellow. Details from the RSC summary of this paper ('The monks' tales').

manuscripts.name: Durham Gospels
manuscripts.notes: Yellow, used extensively. Also reported by Beeby, Durham University.

manuscripts.name: Codex Rossanensis
manuscripts.notes: Yellow, found only on these 2 pages. Everywhere else the yellow is goethite.

pigments.name: Red Lead
pigments.description: Lead tetroxide (Pb3O4), also called minium. A bright orange-red made by roasting lead white, and the standard red of early medieval manuscripts.

manuscripts.name: Book of Kells
manuscripts.notes: Red-orange.

manuscripts.name: Lindisfarne Gospels
manuscripts.notes: Orange and red. Details from the RSC summary of this paper ('The monks' tales').

manuscripts.name: Durham Gospels
manuscripts.notes: Orange and red, mixed with massicot. Also reported by Beeby, Durham University.

manuscripts.name: Book of Durrow
manuscripts.notes: Red. Reported only on a facsimile dealer's page; not independently verified.

manuscripts.name: Codex Rossanensis
manuscripts.notes: Main red. Mixed with goethite for orange and with lead white for pink.

pigments.name: Massicot
pigments.description: Lead monoxide (PbO), a pale yellow. It often occurs alongside red lead as a by-product of making it.

manuscripts.name: Durham Gospels
manuscripts.notes: Mixed with red lead in the oranges and reds.

pigments.name: Indigo
pigments.description: Plant-derived blue; in Insular manuscripts it most likely comes from woad (Isatis tinctoria), and it is chemically identical to indigo from Indigofera. Raman analysis showed it, not lapis lazuli, is the blue of Kells and Lindisfarne.

manuscripts.name: Book of Kells
manuscripts.notes: Blue.

manuscripts.name: Book of Armagh
manuscripts.notes: Blue.

manuscripts.name: Lindisfarne Gospels
manuscripts.notes: The only blue used. It overturns the 1960 identification as lazurite.

manuscripts.name: Codex Rossanensis
manuscripts.notes: Blue. Also mixed with goethite for greens.

pigments.name: Vergaut
pigments.description: Not a single pigment: a green made by mixing indigo with orpiment, typical of the Insular palette.

manuscripts.name: Book of Kells
manuscripts.notes: Green.

manuscripts.name: Lindisfarne Gospels
manuscripts.notes: Green, alongside verdigris. Details from the RSC summary of this paper ('The monks' tales').

manuscripts.name: Codex Rossanensis
manuscripts.notes: Dark, brilliant green on 2 pages only.

pigments.name: Verdigris
pigments.description: Copper acetate, a synthetic blue-green made by exposing copper to vinegar fumes. It can eat through parchment over time.

manuscripts.name: Lindisfarne Gospels
manuscripts.notes: Green, alongside vergaut.

manuscripts.name: Durham Gospels
manuscripts.notes: Green, used instead of vergaut. Beeby's Durham University page says only 'copper-derived green'.

manuscripts.name: Book of Durrow
manuscripts.notes: Green ('copper acetate'). Reported only on a facsimile dealer's page; not independently verified.

pigments.name: Copper Resinate
pigments.description: A transparent green made by dissolving copper salts in resin or oil. McCrone reported the Voynich greens as a copper and copper-chlorine resinate.

manuscripts.name: Voynich Manuscript
manuscripts.notes: Bright and dull greens. Contains a copper organic complex, with atacamite possible on f26r and probable on f47r and f78r.

pigments.name: Azurite
pigments.description: Basic copper carbonate.

manuscripts.name: Voynich Manuscript
manuscripts.notes: Blue flower (f26r) and blue water (f78r), with minor cuprite. Report wording: 'unambiguously identified as ground azurite'.

pigments.name: Red Ochre
pigments.description: Iron oxide (hematite).

manuscripts.name: Voynich Manuscript
manuscripts.notes: Red-brown plant roots. Hematite with lead compounds, and possibly palmierite on f47r.

pigments.name: Yellow Ochre
pigments.description: Iron oxide-hydroxide (goethite).

manuscripts.name: Codex Rossanensis
manuscripts.notes: Identified as goethite. The main yellow throughout, also mixed with lapis lazuli or indigo for greens and with red lead for orange.

pigments.name: Ultramarine Blue
pigments.description: Natural ultramarine ground from lapis lazuli (the blue mineral is lazurite). In this period the only source was Afghanistan, so finding it implies long-distance trade.

manuscripts.name: Codex Rossanensis
manuscripts.notes: Blue. Also mixed with goethite for greens and with red pigments or pink lake for violets.

manuscripts.name: Symeon of Durham, Libellus de exordio
manuscripts.notes: Blue highlight. Also reported by the RSC's 'The monks' tales'.

pigments.name: Vermilion
pigments.description: Mercury sulphide (HgS). 'Cinnabar' is the natural mineral and 'vermilion' usually the synthetic form. It was more expensive than red lead.

manuscripts.name: Codex Rossanensis
manuscripts.notes: Natural cinnabar, used once: for the name 'Markos'.

manuscripts.name: Symeon of Durham, Libellus de exordio
manuscripts.notes: Red.

pigments.name: Elderberry Lake
pigments.description: A pink-violet lake pigment made from elderberry (Sambucus nigra). The Codex Rossanensis is the first experimental evidence of its use in a 6th-century manuscript.

manuscripts.name: Codex Rossanensis
manuscripts.notes: Pink. Also mixed with lapis lazuli for violet.

pigments.name: Orchil
pigments.description: A purple dye from lichens (Roccella species); its colouring compounds are orceins. It was a cheaper substitute for shellfish (Tyrian) purple.

manuscripts.name: Codex Rossanensis
manuscripts.notes: Purple dye of the parchment itself.

manuscripts.name: Book of Kells
manuscripts.notes: The purple is discussed as orcein; the abstract does not say how firm the identification is.

pigments.name: Lead White
pigments.description: Basic lead carbonate. It can darken over time.

manuscripts.name: Lindisfarne Gospels
manuscripts.notes: White, pink and beige, with chalk.

manuscripts.name: Codex Rossanensis
manuscripts.notes: The only white, also used to lighten other colours. It has darkened in the Canon Table miniature.

pigments.name: Chalk
pigments.description: Calcium carbonate (CaCO3).

manuscripts.name: Lindisfarne Gospels
manuscripts.notes: White, and in pinks and beiges with lead white.

pigments.name: Gypsum
pigments.description: Calcium sulphate (CaSO4·2H2O).

manuscripts.name: Book of Kells
manuscripts.notes: White. Also reported by Trinity College Dublin Library.

manuscripts.name: Huexotzinco Codex
manuscripts.notes: White.

pigments.name: Carbon Black
pigments.description: Soot or lamp black: nearly pure carbon.

manuscripts.name: Book of Kells
manuscripts.notes: Black, in one area of design. Also reported by Trinity College Dublin Library.

manuscripts.name: Codex Rossanensis
manuscripts.notes: Black paint and original black inks.

pigments.name: Iron Gall Ink
pigments.description: Ink made from oak galls and iron sulphate (vitriol) in gum. It turns brown, and can corrode the support, as it ages.

manuscripts.name: Book of Kells
manuscripts.notes: Main ink. Also reported by Trinity College Dublin Library.

manuscripts.name: Voynich Manuscript
manuscripts.notes: Text and drawing inks. Critics argue the instruments could not positively identify iron gall.

manuscripts.name: Book of Durrow
manuscripts.notes: Black and brown inks. Reported only on a facsimile dealer's page; not independently verified.

pigments.name: Maya Blue
pigments.description: Indigo locked into a clay mineral (palygorskite and/or sepiolite) by heating, which makes it extremely stable. It is often called the first nanocomposite material in history.

manuscripts.name: Huexotzinco Codex
manuscripts.notes: Made with a mix of palygorskite and sepiolite. The same combination is otherwise known only on the Codex Borgia.

pigments.name: Maya Yellow
pigments.description: An organic yellow dye fixed onto a mineral support, made like Maya blue.

manuscripts.name: Huexotzinco Codex
manuscripts.notes: The mineral support is proposed to be tizatl, a siliceous aquatic alga.

pigments.name: Cochineal Lake
pigments.description: A crimson lake made from the dye of the cochineal insect (Dactylopius coccus) precipitated with alum.

manuscripts.name: Huexotzinco Codex
manuscripts.notes: Alum-based cochineal lake, found on all seven coloured paintings.

pigments.name: Orange Kaolinite
pigments.description: An orange clay (kaolinite) used as a pigment. Its use points to colonial rather than pre-Hispanic practice.

manuscripts.name: Huexotzinco Codex
manuscripts.notes: Orange.
